speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To understand the severity and location of the issue, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been developing and if you have noticed any weakness or numbness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kennedy's Disease (Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy). The combination of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, and bulbar symptoms (speech slurring) in a 54-year-old male is highly characteristic. The chronicity and specific pattern of lower motor neuron signs affecting both limbs and bulbar muscles point toward this diagnosis rather than ALS or cervical myelopathy.
